proof:
# Four simplex peak fibers: exact crossover and a near-plateau bound

Let d>=2, Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, and let lambda=lambda_d be the sharp
subset coefficient proved in
`candidate bb74919333cc624f`. Define

    t=lambda/Gamma,  R=2t-1,  kappa=2d/(d+1),  p=d-1.     (1)

Here t>1, since the older subset coefficient 1/2 is valid and
Gamma<1/2. Let V be the volume of the reference d-simplex. Consider
four actual compatible positively homothetic simplex fibers with
radii

    (a,b,1,c),  0<a<=2b-1,  1/2<b<=1,  0<c<=b.          (2)

This is the opposite endpoint order to the all-dimensional theorem
in `candidate 8f194c2219f76d2a`.
Put M=(a^d+b^d+1+c^d)V and

    J=(1-R^(-1/p))^(-p),
    eta_d=(1-R^(-1/p))*[d(t-1)/(t*kappa^d)]^(1/p).         (3)

The two actual middle centroids obey the quantitative bound

    max(depth_abs(y_1),depth_abs(y_2))
      >= Gamma*M/2
          + Gamma*V/(2t)*[(t-1)(1-b^d)
                              -t*J*(kappa(1-b))^d].     (4)

Consequently the required normalized depth Gamma/2 is attained at
one of these centroids whenever

    (1-b)/b <= eta_d.                                   (5)

This is an explicit all-dimensional regime, uniform in both endpoint
radii. In dimension 2, eta_2=81/280, so (5) is b>=280/361; the full
two-dimensional peak result is already stronger. In higher dimensions
this gives a proved near-equal-middle range. No claim that (5) is
necessary, or that all four-fiber profiles are settled, is made.

## 1. Actual all-cap bounds

For common-vertex fibers aT,bT,T,cT, retain the first three fibers
and shear their middle centroid and larger endpoint centroid to zero.
Exactly as in the three-fiber subset proof, the transformed small
endpoint lies inside b(T-g_T). Applying the sharp subset theorem
therefore gives, in units of V,

    depth_abs(y_1)/V >= L_1=Gamma*b^d+lambda*a^d.          (6)

For the last triple, let K=T-g_T and shear the middle and the larger
endpoint bK to have centroid zero. The other endpoint intersects bK
in a translate of hT, where

    h=[c-kappa(1-b)]_+.

The subset theorem applied to this intersection and two copies of
bK, plus the actual concentric remainder K\bK in the middle, gives

    depth_abs(y_2)/V >= L_2=Gamma+lambda*h^d.             (7)

The intersection calculation is the d-dimensional one in Section 1
of `candidate 8f194c2219f76d2a`,
with its r=c and s=b. The middle remainder contributes exactly
1-b^d times each cap of K through its centroid, hence at least
Gamma(1-b^d)V. Closed vertical caps also satisfy (6)-(7): their
whole-fiber mass is at least b^d+a^d at y_1 and 1+c^d at y_2,
whereas Gamma,lambda<=1 and h<=c. Each containing cap contains a
parallel through-cap.

These are actual one-normal, one-tilt cap inequalities. For arbitrary
compatible translations, the simultaneous own-centroid comparison in
`candidate 24467ade6f021ae8`
transfers both lower bounds to the two actual centroids.

## 2. Sharp scalar loss and the uniform bound

For every x>=0 and every alpha>1,

    sup_(v>=0){v^d-alpha[v-x]_+^d}
       = x^d(1-alpha^(-1/p))^(-p).                      (8)

When x>0 the supremum is attained at

    v=x/(1-alpha^(-1/p)).

To prove this, for v<=x the expression is increasing. For v>x its
derivative has the sign of v^p-alpha(v-x)^p, which vanishes exactly
at the displayed v, is positive before it and negative afterwards.
Substitution gives (8). For x=0 the supremum is zero, attained at
v=0. Thus the scalar constant in (8) is exact; it is not a sampled
or asymptotic bound.

Put A=a^d, B=b^d, C=c^d and H=h^d. Taking the convex combination
of L_1/Gamma and L_2/Gamma with weights 1/(2t),1-1/(2t) cancels A
after subtracting half the total mass. It gives exactly

    max(L_1,L_2)/Gamma -(A+B+1+C)/2
       >= [(t-1)(1-B)-t*C+t*R*H]/(2t).                 (9)

Apply (8) with x=kappa(1-b), alpha=R and v=c. This proves (4).
Finally,

    1-b^d=(1-b)(1+b+...+b^(d-1))
            >=d(1-b)b^(d-1).

For b<1, condition (5), raised to the power p, is exactly sufficient
to make the square bracket in (4) nonnegative. The case b=1 is
immediate directly from (4). This proves the stated geometric result.

The scalar loss in (8) ignores the upper restriction c<=b. Retaining
that restriction improves its supremum to

    J*x^d,                         if x<=b(1-R^(-1/p)),
    b^d-R[b-x]_+^d,                otherwise.            (10)

Either expression may replace J*x^d in (4); formula (10) follows
from the same derivative calculation and is exact on 0<=c<=b.

## 3. Exact optimization of the endpoint volume and crossover

For clarity, the complete scalar certificate admits an explicit
finite minimization at each fixed b. This records where convexity
does and does not permit an endpoint reduction.

Fix b in (1/2,1), let

    A_max=(2b-1)^d,  B=b^d,  x=kappa(1-b),
    S=1-B,  Z=A_max-S/t.

For fixed c and H=[c-x]_+^d define the normalized certificate gap

    G(A,c)=max(B+t*A,1+t*H)-(A+B+1+c^d)/2,
              0<=A<=A_max.

The first line in the maximum has positive slope after the subtraction
and the second has negative slope. The minimizer is therefore

    A_hat=min(A_max,H+S/t).                              (11)

An exact identity, valid also at the crossover, is

    2 min_A G(A,c)
      = -c^d+max{S-A_max+2t*H, (1-1/t)S+R*H}.           (12)

Indeed the two affine expressions on the right differ by H-Z; their
dominance is precisely the choice in (11).

If x>=b, H=0 throughout 0<=c<=b and the minimum of (12) is at c=b.
Suppose x<b. On 0<=c<=x the expression decreases with c, so it is
enough to consider c>=x. Set

    H_max=(b-x)^d,  c=(H^(1/d)+x),  0<=H<=H_max.

The map H -> c^d is concave. For H>0 its derivative is

    (1+x/H^(1/d))^p,

strictly decreasing from infinity to 1. The right side of (12) is
therefore convex in H, with derivative

    R-(1+x/H^(1/d))^p,     when H<Z,
    2t-(1+x/H^(1/d))^p,   when H>Z.

At H=Z the derivative jumps upwards by 1. Define the two exact
stationary values

    H_alpha=x^d/(alpha^(1/p)-1)^d,
    H_(2t)<H_R.

The minimizing H is

    H_hat=min(H_max, max(H_(2t), min(Z,H_R))).            (13)

This includes all boundary cases. Equivalently, take the median of
H_(2t), Z and H_R, then clip to [0,H_max]. Substituting (13) in
(12) is the exact minimum of the proposed scalar certificate over
all 0<=a<=2b-1 and 0<=c<=b, with b fixed. Positive endpoints are
recovered by restriction or limits. The case b=1, x=0 is handled
directly by (12) and has nonnegative gap.

This formula exposes the possible interior minima rather than
incorrectly checking only endpoints of convex functions. It is an
exact scalar identity, not an assertion that its value is nonnegative
for every b and every dimension. Formula (4) is the proved uniform
lower estimate extracted here. Beyond the previously proved ordered
endpoint case and the explicit condition (5), no all-dimensional
four-fiber conclusion is claimed.

## 4. Exact verification

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_four_simplex_peak_crossover_bound.py` uses rational parameters
R=q^(-(d-1)), t=(1+R)/2, so the sharp loss constant J is rational.
It verifies (8), (9), the exact endpoint-volume crossover, and the
near-plateau implication in several dimensions without floating-point
comparisons. These scalar identities hold for every t>1. To apply them
geometrically, t is specifically the sharp coefficient in (1).
